newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGT union seeks withdrawal of SNCF rail reform law.
newsitem.headline: CGT union seeks withdrawal of SNCF rail reform law.

text.p: France's communist-led CGT trade union called on Monday for the withdrawal of draft legislation which would change the structure of the SNCF state railways by creating a separate rail infrastructure company.

The union published a letter to transport minister Bernard Pons in which it called for the withdrawal of the draft law "so that new proposals can be drawn up which meet the expectations of users and railworkers".
It said the draft legislation did not live up to what had been promised by the government in its proposals for the reform of the SNCF last June.

The union said the SNCF reform debate opened in the wake of last year's rail strikes had been hijacked in the end to push through changes which would fit in with European Commission's calls for deregulation of national rail network management in the European Union.

The law in question concerns the creation of a state company which would become owner of France's rail infrastructure and also take over 125 billion francs of SNCF debts which exceed 200 billion francs. The government has said SNCF would keep control of infrastructure management under the new split structure.

The CGT said the state was pursuing a line of gradually getting out of financial commitment to the SNCF and that the financing of the future infrastructure owner as well as its relations with the SNCF as a rail operator were far from clear.
